Round 88 fails. The sticky footer works, but one medium keyboard bug fails two of B's acceptance rows. Every browser check that can run in the cloud ran at both 1440×900 and 1280×720, so `browserVerified` and `realVerified` are true.

**The footer fix works.**
- **During exports:** the status line, progress label, progress bar and busy button were fully visible and clickable in every sample of every phase (render, WAV write, encoder load, MP3) at both viewports.
- **No self-scroll:** the panel never scrolled by itself during an export.
- **Old cut fixed:** the export button no longer loses its bottom 12 px at 1280.
- **Scrolling (1280):** I scrolled the panel to its maximum (145 px) and back during a render. The footer stayed visible and covered nothing.
- **Scrolling (1440):** this check doesn't apply, because the panel has nothing to scroll.
- **Done, error and video states:** the done message and overload warning, the encoder-failure alert, and the video-clip dialog were all fully visible. Their texts match round 87.
- **No covered focus:** a focused control was never hidden behind the footer. The new focus guard really fired at 1280, scrolling the panel 27 px to show a radio.

**The bug: R88-FOCUS-ESCAPE-RENDER (medium).** While an export is rendering, keyboard focus escapes the Export dialog.
- **What happens:** with WAV (the default) or MP3 selected, the third Tab press leaves the dialog. Focus then reaches the exit link and the Master Mute and Master Volume controls behind the busy dialog, so Space or Enter there would act on the workspace mid-export.
- **When:** at both viewports, including the exact round-87 recipe. With WAV + MP3 selected, focus correctly wraps back to the close button.
- **Not caused by this round:** the focus-trap code is identical to the round-87 version. Round 87's keyboard check only passed because its render had already finished by the third Tab.
- **Likely cause** (my reading of the code, consistent with what I saw):
  - During a render the only enabled controls are the close button and the format radios.
  - The trap only wraps when focus is on the last radio, "WAV + MP3".
  - Tab treats a radio group as one stop, so it leaves the dialog from any other selected radio.
